summary: People call it an "absolute visual spectacle," and that is the easiest honest pitch. It is chilly, majestic, and built more like an experience than a plot machine, which makes it great when the room wants to lock into pure movie magic.
good_pick_if: You want something huge, hypnotic, and genuinely transportive.
maybe_skip_if: You need brisk pacing or a movie that explains itself along the way.

summary: The appeal is how "thought-provoking" and eerie it feels without ever turning academic. It is a sleek identity spiral with just enough science-fiction strangeness to keep the whole thing unsettling.
good_pick_if: You want a cerebral, moody movie that still has real tension in it.
maybe_skip_if: You want a warmer character drama or something less abstract.

summary: People call it a "concept-laden tearjerker," and that is still the lane. It is romantic, messy, funny, and emotionally bruised in a way that feels more human than precious.
good_pick_if: You want something imaginative that still lands like a real breakup movie.
maybe_skip_if: You want a lighter romance or something less emotionally raw.

summary: People call it "a dream alive on the screen," which gets at why it still works. It is gigantic, stylish, and weirdly alive, the kind of silent sci-fi landmark that can still make a room go wow.
good_pick_if: You want a foundational classic that still feels bold and visually overwhelming.
maybe_skip_if: You want something subtle, intimate, or less openly monumental.

summary: People call it an "original, inventive & ambitious" sci-fi wonder, and that is pretty much the movie-night case. It is slick, propulsive, and complicated in a fun way that keeps the whole room leaning in.
good_pick_if: You want a blockbuster that feels smart, polished, and easy to get swept up in.
maybe_skip_if: You want something looser, stranger, or less mechanics-heavy.

summary: The sell is that it "hangs on to memory" instead of just doing space spectacle. It is patient, mournful, and better treated as a haunted emotional drift than a conventional sci-fi story.
good_pick_if: You want thoughtful, melancholy science fiction with real emotional weight.
maybe_skip_if: You want action, urgency, or a cleaner narrative path.

summary: People call it "wildly entertaining," and that is exactly how to pitch it. It is a blood-slick revenge spectacle with movie-star swagger, killer music, and enough formal play to keep it from feeling disposable.
good_pick_if: You want something loud, fun, and incredibly sure of its own cool.
maybe_skip_if: You want emotional subtlety or have low tolerance for graphic violence.

summary: The big draw is the "heartfelt charm" running through the whole thing. It is soft, visually lovely, and built to hit both kids and adults without feeling smug about it.
good_pick_if: You want an emotional animated crowd-pleaser that still feels sincere.
maybe_skip_if: You want sharper comedy or something less openly sentimental.

summary: People call it a "beautiful canvas of tragedy and comedy," which gets at why it sticks. It starts like a mystery, then opens into something much sadder and more human about friendship across a line that should not exist.
good_pick_if: You want a gripping drama that is tense, moving, and very easy to talk about after.
maybe_skip_if: You want something lighter or less politically charged.

summary: People call it an "astounding and spectacular" animated film, and it earns that. It has adventure energy, giant imagination, and a real moral pulse, which makes it feel both sweeping and deeply sincere.
good_pick_if: You want a fantasy adventure with scope, urgency, and one of animation's great heroes.
maybe_skip_if: You want something cozier and less war-shaped in its stakes.
